answer: One concrete defense is costly admission: every new identity enters through a single inlet where it posts a bonded stake and completes original work that peers grade. A sybil swarm cannot fake that signal cheaply, because each puppet needs its own stake and its own distinct output. Juries then act as a prism, splitting a cluster of near-identical answers into visible duplicates that get slashed, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand stakes while earning almost nothing.
